questions.question: Compare the suffragists and the suffragettes.
questions.expected_answer: Suffrage is the right to vote. The suffragists of the NUWSS, formed in 1897 and led by Millicent Fawcett, used peaceful, lawful methods such as petitions, meetings, lobbying and marches, and became the largest organisation. The suffragettes of the WSPU, founded in 1903 in Manchester by Emmeline Pankhurst with Christabel and Sylvia, used the motto Deeds, not words and militant methods: interrupting meetings, chaining themselves to railings, smashing windows, arson and hunger strikes. Militancy brought publicity but may have hardened opposition.

questions.question: Describe Emmeline Pankhurst's role and the government's response to the suffragettes.
questions.expected_answer: Emmeline Pankhurst, born in Manchester in 1858, founded the WSPU in 1903, led its militant campaign and was imprisoned many times. From 1909 hunger strikers were force-fed, and the 1913 Cat and Mouse Act released weak hunger strikers and re-arrested them after recovery. Emily Wilding Davison died after being struck by the king's horse at the 1913 Derby. In 1914 Pankhurst halted militancy, backed the war, recruited for it and led the 1915 right to serve march, while Sylvia Pankhurst opposed the war. She died on 14 June 1928, weeks before equal franchise became law.

questions.question: Explain how the First World War contributed to women gaining the vote.
questions.expected_answer: Women's war work showed their capability and changed opponents' minds; the need to reform voting rules so that soldiers overseas could vote created an opportunity to include women; Lloyd George replaced Asquith in 1916; and a Speaker's Conference recommended reform in 1917. The Representation of the People Act of February 1918 gave the vote to all men over 21 and women over 30 meeting a property qualification, about 8.4 million women, about 39 percent of voters, though many young munitions workers were excluded. Women could stand for Parliament from 1918, Nancy Astor sat from 1919, and the 1928 act gave women equal voting at 21.
